title: The 10 s admission durability fence fails when TermAl's state writer stalls, retaining the prompt and pausing the session (root of PI-32 and PI-34 occurrences)
outcome: After Engram grants and begins a turn, TermAl checks that its own state is durable before delivery (confirm_engram_admission_durable, src/engram_queued_admission.rs:347-398). The check asks the local SQLite writer to save the session and read it back, within admission start + ENGRAM_DISPATCH_BUDGET_MS (10 000 ms, src/engram_host_adapter.rs:16). When it misses that deadline, engram_host_adapter.rs:4732-4758 calls interrupt_queued_engram_admission. That retains the prompt, blocks auto-dispatch, shows "Engram: interrupted/unknown delivery. Prompt retained; cancel or reconcile before continuing." and drops the session to Idle. TermAl then sends Engram an exit checkpoint keyed termal-stale-begin-checkpoint:<session>:<grant>. Engram answered every call in the observed cases, so the stall is inside TermAl. What stalls the writer for 10 s is unproved: disk contention from concurrent gates, a write retry backoff, or the state lock held elsewhere. No timing is logged.
acceptance: A missed admission durability deadline under host load does not leave a session silently paused: either the check is retried or reconciled once the writer recovers (the grant's begin is known to Engram), or the paused state is named to the session's senders (PI-32's cheap half)
TermAl logs, for each admission durability check, how long the save and the read-back took and what the writer was waiting on, so a missed deadline names its cause
The cause of the observed 10 s stalls is identified from that logging and fixed or bounded, with a regression test for the chosen behaviour
